title: Drinking Contest
text: “Well, it does seem like things get complicated when Yuki-chan drinks. In multiple senses.”
“Is that so?”

“Yeah. Like… if she drove solo while under the influence, that wouldn’t be a laughing matter, would it? Actually, now I’m wondering—if Motoyasu-kun drinks while riding in a carriage, is that drunk driving? Or is it drunk driving if Yuki-chan drinks? Which is it?”
“Wouldn’t it be Yuki-san? I mean, that person’s just riding along, so—well, if she sprouted wheels and started moving on her own, that’d definitely be a problem.”
Rabbit Guy answered Father’s question in a drunken sort of way, indeed.
“I… see.”
“Well then, let’s keep going!”
“Woof! A toast to everyone coming to my territory!”

Gulp, gulp—at Wolf’s call, we all kept right on drinking. More and more bottles kept getting carried in, and everyone kept up the raucous revelry, I say. And then, thud—Rabbit Guy, thoroughly drunk, collapsed onto the floor. Whether it was inexperience or what, he was the first to go down. Right up until the end he’d been cackling away.
“Zzz…”
“Looks like Teo’s out cold. Well, he’s not exactly a seasoned drinker, so I suppose that’s only natural.”
“Woof! One down!”
Wolf struck a victory pose. Father gently draped a blanket over the sleeping Rabbit Guy.
“Still sleeping in his rabbit form, huh. Is there some rule where demi-humans and beastmen revert to their true form when they pass out drunk?”
Father asked Panda, remarking that sleeping Teo’s face looked kind of cute.

“Ahn? Depends on the person, I s’pose. Booze restores magic power, so some folks end up shiftin’ into their beast form from the extra strength surgin’ through ’em, while others transform just from relaxin’.”
“I see, so it’s not necessarily about the alcohol stripping away a disguise, then.”
“If it were a monster, now, that’d be a different story—their disguise’d come right off, they say.”
“I see, so that’s the difference between demi-humans and monsters, more or less.”
“Still drinkin’! Wooof!”
“Hmph. I won’t let things go your way. Not that it matters how hard you try to get someone drunk who simply doesn’t get drunk.”
“Woof. Once the night wears on, if nothin’ else happens, sleepiness’ll get him eventually. Wolf’ll just wait it out.”
“I see… clever.”
Crackling with tension, Crocodile Guy and Wolf glared at each other while downing drink after drink. Meanwhile, Yuki-chan—
“Yes, Motoyasu-sama! Please, have some more!”
It was lovely that she kept pouring more and more sake into my cup, determined not to be outdone, but if I drank too much I’d end up drunk myself, indeed.
“I shall drink!”
Still, I had to live up to Yuki-chan’s expectations. Meanwhile, Father was busy poking at sleeping Rabbit Guy’s peacefully smiling whiskers, playing with them.
“No sign of him throwing up, so I guess that’s a healthy way to pass out. Teo’s gotten pretty sturdy, hasn’t he.”
He was the weakest drinker of the bunch, true, but he wasn’t exactly a lightweight either—there seemed to be room for him to grow, indeed.
“Puhaa! Woof!”
“Still more!”
Wolf and Crocodile Guy kept gulping it down without end.
“Well, I guess Shion’s got some stress built up too, huh? That’s an unusual way for him to drink. Eclair-san doesn’t drink that much either.”
“Sir Knight once lost a territory management contest to Elmelo and got so drunk complainin’ about it he passed clean out.”
“Ah, so that explains the time I saw him drinking with Lars-chan. Still, both Wolf and Shion are holding out pretty well, aren’t they.”
The room was already littered with empty bottles.
“Still, in a way, this kind of feels fun, like we’re all on some big trip together.”
“I got a feelin’ you might be the only one thinkin’ that, y’know.”
“You think? Oh, you two shouldn’t just drink alcohol on its own, that’s not great for you—eat something along with it, alright?”
“Woooof.”
“Understood.”
They’d brought over some leftovers to serve as drinking snacks, indeed.
“Still, I gotta say, having a fun banquet with a werewolf and a lizardman in some Western fantasy castle—there’s a certain atmosphere to that, isn’t there.”
Father seemed to be thoroughly enjoying this whole exchange.
“Looks like I don’t need an escort back to my room this time.”
“Zzz… Iwatani-sama, mmph mmph…”
Using the sleeping Rabbit Guy as a backrest, Father kept right on drinking with Panda, indeed.
“Makin’ merry all night in the head of household’s own room—I’d love to see what the clan makes of that.”
“Woof! No problem!”
Wolf declared this firmly, cup raised toward Panda. Since this was a banquet welcoming Shield Hero-sama, I suppose everything was simply excused.
“Woof! Push-ups, fifty, speed round!”
“Hmph! Challenge accepted! Spear Hero too!”
Wolf and Crocodile Guy were competing, with the rule being that whoever lost had to drink, indeed.
“I shall not lose! Full power!”
Push-ups, indeed! Shaking with the effort!
“Wow, he’s completely drunk, huh.”
“Do more, y’hear.”
Panda clapped enthusiastically.
“So, what exactly are you doin’ with me here.”
“Eh? Well, just trying accessories that might suit a pleasantly tipsy Lars-chan?”
“Tch, guess it can’t be helped.”
Panda, now in good spirits, let Father festoon her with various accessories, indeed.
“I achieved fifty first, indeed!”
I was the winner of this round’s push-up contest, indeed.
“As expected of Motoyasu-sama! Here, have some!”
“Right then! Gulp gulp… wait? Yuki-chan, since I won, I don’t need to drink any…more…do I, indeed?”

Whether Yuki-chan won or lost, she kept right on pressing more sake on me, indeed. That won’t do, Yuki-chan. At this rate I’d lose to Wolf and the others. Well, since Wolf and company were losing too and drinking as penance, it ought to even out somehow, indeed. And so the night wore on and on, and Father’s yawns grew more frequent until he started to nod off. Father usually stayed up without sleeping much, but in a setting like this, perhaps boredom got the better of him and he started dozing off. Meanwhile, ignoring Father entirely, the contest between me, Crocodile Guy, and Wolf continued. We kept gulping away, determined not to lose, but tonight Wolf was strangely strong. Before he could even speak, Wolf—usually the type to cry drunk and tie a bandana round his head, tearing it apart—just kept right on with the contest.
“Guh… not yet… kuuuh.”
Having lost some small bout, Crocodile Guy drank valiantly straight from the barrel.
“Uoooooh!”
“Motoyasu-sama! Amazing, truly! Here, one more!”
“Uugh… Yuki-chan, when I win I don’t need to drink, indeed.”

Occasionally, even when Yuki-chan won, she’d beg me to drink anyway—which was quite a demanding ordeal, indeed. I felt like I’d been about to pass out before too, but I couldn’t bear to make Yuki-chan sad. Draw lots, rock-paper-scissors, card games—the contests just kept coming, indeed. Win or lose, we were all roughly even. It was really just a matter of who could hold their liquor better in the end.
“Zzzz…”
Father was already fast asleep, leaning against Rabbit Guy and Panda. Panda seemed to be smiling gently down at sleeping Father leaning on her—or was that just my imagination?
“Heh heh, now that’s got some spirit to it.”

Panda, content to watch from the sidelines like some spectator at a high vantage point, drank along after every single round, yet showed no sign whatsoever of passing out. Excluding Father, Older Sister was monstrously strong when it came to drinking, but Panda was quite formidable too, indeed. Drinking herself under the table seemed to trigger some kind of mode change in her, but perhaps she simply hadn’t reached that threshold yet.
